final_answer:
Cell-cell communication analysis of scRNA-seq data from celiac disease intestinal mucosa (GSE193442, 72,172 cells from 6 CeD + 4 HC donors) identified two principal non-MHC-I signaling pathways by which KIR+CD8+ T cells are predicted to mediate suppressive function toward CD4+ T cells, ranked by LIANA consensus specificity score with 1,000-permutation null:

1. Galectin-1 (LGALS1) signaling — TOP PREDICTED PATHWAY
   - Ligand: LGALS1 (galectin-1), expressed by 62-91% of KIR+CD8+ T cells (mean expr 1.42-2.29)
   - Receptors on CD4+ T cells: CD69 (58.7%), ITGB1 (57.5%), PTPRC/CD45 (82-86%)
   - Highest specificity: KIR3DL1+ → CD4_T_EM_gut (LGALS1→CD69, spec_rank=0.0338)
   - Mechanism: Galectin-1 is a well-established immunomodulatory lectin known to induce apoptosis of activated Th1/Th17 CD4+ T cells via CD45/CD7 cross-linking, suppress IFN-gamma and IL-17 production, and promote T cell tolerance (Perillo et al. 1995 Nature; Toscano et al. 2007 Nat Immunol).

2. SPON2 (Spondin-2/Mindin) signaling
   - Ligand: SPON2, expressed by 39-62% of KIR+CD8+ T cells (highest in multi-KIR+ subset, 62.1%)
   - Receptors on CD4+ T cells: ITGB1 (57.5%), ITGA4 (29.9%), ITGB2 (75.7%)
   - Highest specificity: multi-KIR+ → CD4_T_EM_gut (SPON2→ITGB1, spec_rank=0.1174, magn_rank=1.0)
   - Mechanism: SPON2 is an ECM protein that functions as a pattern-recognition molecule for integrin-mediated immune cell adhesion and may facilitate KIR+CD8+ T cell recruitment and contact-dependent regulation of CD4+ T cells at inflammatory sites.

The established MHC-I/KIR interaction (HLA-A/B/C/B2M → KIR2DL1/KIR3DL1) was confirmed as the most specific overall interaction but was exclusively observed between KIR+CD8+ cells themselves (self-interaction), not from KIR+CD8+ to CD4+ T cells (which lack KIR receptors).

Additionally, KIR+CD8+ T cells universally express high levels of CCL5 (100% of cells) and CCL4 (72-77%), which may attract CD4+ T cells via CCR1/CCR5 to facilitate these contact-dependent signaling interactions. The multi-KIR+/IFNGhigh subset (cluster 20, 87.4% KIR+CD8+, 98% CeD) is the most functionally specialized, showing the highest KIR co-expression, highest IFNG (11.7%), and highest SPON2 expression, suggesting it is the dominant effector population mediating CD4+ T cell regulation via both LGALS1 and SPON2 pathways.
